newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ERASMUS BLASTS RAPID 67 TO SEND ENGLAND REELING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ERASMUS BLASTS RAPID 67 TO SEND ENGLAND REELING.

text.p: A Zimbabwe President's X1 containing nine test players handed out an emphatic five-wicket defeat to England in the second one-day match of their tour at the Harare Sports Club on Sunday.
Dannie Erasmus, one of the non-test players in the home side, struck four sixes and seven fours in a 60-ball 67 as the President's X1 raced to victory with 4.1 of their 50 overs to spare.
Zimbabwe test captain Alistair Campbell contributed a painstaking 45 in 98 balls and Craig Evans blasted 17 from nine balls, including two sixes back over the head of paceman Andy Caddick.
The President's side completed victory at 215 for five after England, lifted by 105 from opener Alec Stewart, made 211 for five in their 50 overs.
"It's inconvenient to lose to some President's X1 but the serious stuff hasn't started yet," England coach David Lloyd told reporters.
"Our lads haven't been on a cricket pitch since September and it's understandable that some of them didn't bowl so well, but that's the way of the world and they'll have to get it right."

Caddick sent down nine of England's 16 wides in his 7.5 overs which cost 6.6 an over, as did Ronnie Irani's six overs, while left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell was only marginally less costly as his 10 overs went for 59.
By contrast Mullally bowled his quota of 10 for only 18 runs, and off-spinner Robert Croft was the most successful bowler with two for 29 from his 10 overs.
The other highlight for England was the batting of Stewart, whose patient century prevented an even heavier defeat.
His 133-run fourth-wicket partnership with Nasser Hussain (50) rescued England after they had been put in to bat and reduced to 24 for three.
Eddo Brandes took all three wickets in the space of 13 balls, including that of England skipper Mike Atherton, who went to a fine catch after getting a leading edge to his second delivery.
Stewart took 116 balls to reach his 50 but blossomed thereafter, posting his second half-century in only 36 balls, hitting two sixes and seven fours in his 105.
England are next in action on Tuesday when they begin a four-day match against Mashonoland at the Harare Sports Club.
